name: Harborline Logistics palette
how_to_read: Each colour has a light-mode hex, a dark-mode hex (when it changes), the CSS token, and what it is for. Data-viz slots are validated with the dataviz skill validator (see brand/validation/palette-report.txt).

brand.name: Harbor Navy
brand.usage: Primary brand colour. Logo tile, report header band, primary ink family. Never a chart series.

brand.name: Harbor Teal
brand.usage: Accent: primary buttons, links, selected tab, Operations department. 5.0:1 with white text.

brand.name: Signal Orange
brand.usage: Signal colour from the logo wave. Use under 5% of any screen: one highlight, a callout, the brand mark wave. Text on white must use #C9501C (focus) instead.

brand.name: Sand
brand.usage: Print and slide backgrounds behind the logo. Not a dashboard background (charts are validated on Fog and white).

neutrals.name: Mist (surface 2)
neutrals.usage: Filter rail, table header, hover row, input fill

neutrals.name: Slate (muted text)
neutrals.usage: Labels, captions, axis titles (>= 4.5:1 on every surface)

neutrals.name: Other
neutrals.usage: The folded "Other" series and de-emphasised marks

accent.name: Accent strong
accent.usage: Hover / pressed, accent text on tinted surfaces

status.name: Good
status.usage: On target / healthy. Always with a check icon + the word.

status.name: Warning
status.usage: Watch / near threshold. Always with a triangle icon + the word.

status.name: Bad
status.usage: Off target / breach. Always with a cross or octagon icon + the word.

status.name: Info
status.usage: Neutral notice, data note, freshness message.

categorical_rules: Assign slots in order 1..8 and never cycle. A 9th series folds into "Other" (--hl-viz-other).
Colour follows the entity, not its rank: once a warehouse or client has a slot, keep it on every page.
Scatter, bubble, map and small-multiple charts: at most the first 3 slots (validated all-pairs).
Slot 4 Brass is 2.2:1 on white: when it is used, show data labels or offer the table view.

sequential.usage: Magnitude: heatmaps, filled maps, density. For discrete ordered buckets (tiers, aging buckets) use steps 3-7 only.

diverging.usage: Above / below a reference: variance to budget, forecast error, temperature vs set point. Step 5 is the neutral midpoint. For bars use the outer steps 1-3 and 7-9.

departments.usage: Department identity in chrome only: header stripe, chip, active tab. Never a data series.
